    Isochrones come from a raster cost model at 0.1 mile resolution, not from a routing engine. They show the correct shape — stretched along the freeways, cut off by the bay and the mountains — but each contour can be off by several minutes locally. Speeds are free-flow. Peak-hour contours would be much smaller along US-101 and SR-237. Address pins are geocoded with OpenStreetMap Nominatim (needs internet; you can also type raw “lat, lon”) and placed with a calibrated fit that is typically within ±0.2 mi — treat verdicts near a zone edge as “check closer”. Added addresses persist in this browser via localStorage. Flood (FEMA NFHL), fire (CAL FIRE FHSZ), liquefaction and Alquist-Priolo zones (CGS) are real GIS data fetched Aug 2026 and simplified to map scale; hazard checks count all layers even when a layer is toggled off. City outlines are OSM administrative boundaries. Seven site markers (Newby Island, NTT SV1, San Jose CC, Boulder Ridge, Zanker 1, Palo Alto RWQCP, Moffett golf) were re-audited Aug 2026 and moved 0.4–1 mi to their true locations; corrected buffer circles were added, but the original carved buffer shapes still sit at the old spots. The freeway / El Camino corridor was rebuilt from OSM road centerlines (1000 ft / 500 ft buffers) after the drawn corridor was found to miss ~3 of 4 true freeway-adjacent points; the original corridor shape is retained.
